reason: The cited evidence supports that equiatomic composition promotes uniform dispersion and protective oxide formation (E1, E3), and that these oxides enhance hardness and thermal stability (E2, E3). However, the direct link between uniform lattice distortion and oxide nucleation, the specific role of oxides as wear barriers, and the predicted degradation with non-equiatomic compositions are not directly evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: Equiatomic composition ensures uniform elemental dispersion and inhibits phase separation
Uniform dispersion promotes a homogeneously distorted lattice that favors protective oxide nucleation
Protective oxide phases (e.g., (Fe,Co,Ni,Mn,Cu)3O4) enhance hardness and thermal stability
These oxide layers act as wear barriers, reducing material removal
Non-equiatomic compositions will degrade oxide layer continuity and increase wear
